title: 2014 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: There are exactly \(N\) distinct rational numbers \(k\) such that \(|k|\lt200\) and \[5x^2+kx+12=0\] has at least one integer solution for \(x.\) What is \(N?\)

solutions.text:
If an integer \(x\) is a root, then \(k=-\left(5x+\dfrac{12}{x}\right),\) so \(x\ne0.\) For \(x\ge2,\) \(|k|=5|x|+\dfrac{12}{|x|}\) increases, and \(|x|=39\) gives \(|k|\approx195.3\lt200,\) while \(|x|=40\) gives \(|k|\gt200.\)

Thus \(x\) ranges over \(\pm1,\pm2,\dots,\pm39,\) which is \(78\) values. If two integers \(a\ne b\) gave the same \(k,\) then \(5a+\tfrac{12}{a}=5b+\tfrac{12}{b}\) forces \(5ab=12,\) which has no integer solutions, so all \(78\) values of \(k\) are distinct.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: If \(x\) is an integer root, solve for \(k=-\dfrac{5x^2+12}{x}\) \(=-\left(5x+\dfrac{12}{x}\right)\)
Require \(|k|=5|x|+\dfrac{12}{|x|}\lt200\), and check the resulting values of \(k\) are all distinct
